comments.body:
*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

Yes. Startup loads YAML, but Rust `Default` repeats its values; the existing
equality test detects drift rather than removing that second source. I will make
the committed YAML authoritative through one configuration owner that embeds,
deserializes and validates it once. `TacticalCombatConfig::default()` and the
existing subconfig defaults will project that value, preserving their callers
and values. The inspected deserializers have no `serde(default)` callbacks, and
validation does not read the runtime-config lock, so this route avoids recursive
defaults and lock acquisition. Invalid external YAML stays a fallible startup
error. Invalid compiled-in YAML is an internal invariant failure: `Default`
cannot return an error, so that case will have an explicit panic, with no
`unwrap`, `expect` or numeric fallback. The parser package is already locked;
this requires its tactical-core dependency edge rather than another package
version.

Audit for existing types which can replace these `f32`s. For instance:
* `HeightSpeed` for the height-speed fields guarantees finite, nonnegative metres per second
* `HeightDistance` for the height-distance fields guarantees finite, nonnegative metres
* `AnimationElapsed` for `maximum_frame_seconds` guarantees finite, nonnegative seconds
  * Note that `AnimationElapsed` allows zero, so for a field we divide by (like `smooth_time_seconds`), we want a newtype with a positive smoothing duration contract.
Fields without exact matching owners can have their typing deferred to later PRs.

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

**Preserve the sample identity through posture transitions.** This extracts an already typed tick solely to enter another application API. Change `PostureTransitionState.start_tick` and `dive_landing_tick: Option<u64>` to retain `AnimationSampleTick`, and propagate it through the transition constructor, `begin_posture_transition` and `advance_posture_transition`. Include `apply_posture_action`, `begin_get_up_transition_configured` and the capture callers in `capture.rs` / `capture/subject_motion.rs`, which currently make the same premature extraction. `duration_ticks` remains an interval, not an `AnimationSampleTick`; preserve existing start/landing/recovery timing and saturating arithmetic when introducing the necessary tick/span operations.

See the [producer-propagation rule](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L42).

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

**Use the existing sample-tick owner for the attack-facing deadline.** This `tick`, `AttackFacing.contact_tick` and `begin_attack_facing(contact_tick)` are animation sample coordinates: the contact deadline comes from attack timing, and the current value is the same clock coordinate admitted into `SkeletonLocomotionInput`. Carry `AnimationSampleTick` through the component, constructor, `advance_rotation` and `update_attack_facing_targets`. Admit the numeric value at the native `Time` conversion in the callers, rather than passing raw integers through facing logic and wrapping them only for locomotion. Keep the existing deadline expiration and saturating remaining-time behavior; the difference between the two coordinates is an interval.

See the [producer-propagation rule](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L42).

comments.body:
*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

There are exact matches for the reviewed height measurements, elapsed intervals,
strictly positive metre settings and finite angle coordinates. The height
measurements currently live above core configuration, so I will share their
zero-permitting measurement leaves lower and retain useful height roles.
PositiveLength is suitable only where the current contract already rejects zero.
Smoothing currently accepts zero and the advancing spring divides directly by
it; a positive-duration refinement will intentionally reject zero earlier, while
the zero-elapsed return remains valid. No exact existing general movement-speed
or finite non-unit orientation owner was found: impact speed and height speed
have different roles, and RigidRotation would reject accepted non-unit input. I
will keep those unmatched audit leaves explicit instead of silently narrowing
them. Signed/unwrapped coordinates and scalar wire units remain supported.

comments.body:
*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

**Continue the elapsed-time owner through facing APIs.** `AttackFacing::advance_rotation` accepts `AnimationElapsed`, then erases it before calling `body_turn_speed_for_deadline` and `advance_body_facing_toward`. The shared body/downed-facing APIs also pass `delta_seconds: f32` through several application wrappers. Carry the existing elapsed owner through the deadline helper and the `advance_body_facing*`/`advance_downed_body_facing*` family, admitting engine `Time`/timer values at their original framework boundary. The remaining deadline interval can likewise be a typed span/elapsed value until its calculation. Project seconds at the angular stepping kernel, preserving zero-delta behavior, deadline saturation and the current turn-speed calculation. This request concerns time; it is separate from the existing comment on the downed-roll target/progress fields. See [producer/record guidance](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/376ff773b6d126b46a90f3362bedadee71421bb0/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L57).

comments.body:
*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

**The timing extraction still publishes primitive application values.** `MeleePlaybackTiming` now retains `contact_from_input_seconds: f32`; its constructor accepts three raw durations, `delayed_melee_contact_seconds` returns `(f32, f32)`, and `AttackTarget` retains the same arrival delay as a float. These are internal producers/records before the actual Bevy `Timer` construction. Carry checked elapsed values and a named delay/contact result through that path, extracting seconds at `Timer::from_seconds`; the server's `ingress::timing` also still accepts raw `lunge_delay_seconds`. Trace the shared `melee_lunge_delay_seconds` producer first: it deliberately returns infinity for an unreachable lunge. Preserve that outcome explicitly rather than blindly admitting the sentinel into a finite duration, replacing it with zero, or imposing the server-private `CombatDuration`'s different clamping policy. This is the remaining arrival-duration family; it need not reopen structured error propagation. See [producer/record guidance](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/376ff773b6d126b46a90f3362bedadee71421bb0/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L57).

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

I found no exact existing owner for these two values. The target is a signed, unwrapped downed-roll coordinate in half-turns; `maximum_step` is a nonnegative half-turn increment. `BodyAngle`/`Radians` use radians, and `CyclePhase` uses full cycles. The [current producer](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/0be26d3856c4670207223e5d8786370e948808c6/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/animation/state.rs#L1893) also sanitizes nonfinite targets and invalid steps. I’ll preserve that policy and keep this unmatched coordinate role separate from the elapsed-time migration.

comments.body:
Threat construction now returns `AuthoredThreatResult<Combatant>` and preserves unknown-threat, weapon-timing and sidearm-construction failures, including the weapon recipe’s validation errors. The sidearm no longer uses `expect`. Mission/encounter reducers and simulator bootstrap retain these causes.

The pinned SpacetimeDB SDK accepts `Result<(), E>` where `E: Display`, so reducers keep the typed error and the SDK renders it at the runtime boundary. No first-party `String` adapter is needed.

The shared weapon constructor also serves the iteration roster. Timeline and fatigue evidence now retain timing, performance and battle-resolution causes through the native command’s error. This is published in `596fb3b8778c1461a7831ea1adb65262c9caa933`; [current-head hosted checks](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/774/checks) are pending.
